title: Yoma Mandalay International Marathon: A New Half on the Ayeyarwady
meta_description: Full review of the Yoma Mandalay International Marathon: course, fees, prize money and organisation for this new 21/10/5km race in Mandalay, Myanmar.
dek: Myanmar's biggest running brand brings its half marathon, 10K and 5K to Mandalay for the first time in years, with a second edition now set for December 2026.
verdict: This is a young, ambitious race rather than a polished institution: a debut January 2026 outing at Bahtoo Stadium proved Yoma could pull a crowd and pay out real prize money, and the December 6, 2026 follow-up builds on that. It suits runners who want an urban Southeast Asian half with cultural sightseeing and a straightforward 21/10/5 menu, plus competitive locals chasing kyat prizes. Overseas entrants should watch the official site closely, since the exact start point for this edition hasn't been confirmed yet.

sections.heading: The Course: Downtown Mandalay, Route Still Taking Shape
paragraphs: The debut Mandalay edition in January 2026 started and finished at Bahtoo Stadium, with organisers describing routes that took runners "past iconic sites in Mandalay" [1]. Official notices placed the race under the Mandalay Region Government and confirmed the event and its road closures sat around the downtown grid near Chanayethazan Township [2][6].

That debut closed a tight cluster of numbered streets — stretches of 30th, 29th, 28th, 73rd, 26th, 80th, 12th, 66th and 71st streets — for the morning of the race, which gives a sense of a compact, city-block course rather than a sprawling point-to-point [3].

For the December 6, 2026 edition covered here, the exact start point has not yet been published, so anyone planning travel should treat Bahtoo Stadium as a strong precedent rather than a confirmed venue until the organiser updates the race guide [1].

sections.heading: Organisation, Fees and Logistics
paragraphs: Yoma runs registration entirely online through its own platform, with payments accepted via WavePay, KBZPay, AYA Pay and card networks — a sign the organiser is set up for both local and international entrants [4]. At the debut edition, fee tiers were split by nationality, with local participants required to show identification and anyone without valid ID treated as an international entrant and charged the difference or forced to forfeit their slot [2].

The rulebook is fairly standard for a national-federation-adjacent race: no refunds once payment clears, strict cut-off times with disqualification for stragglers, and doping tests for category winners in the half marathon and challenge run [7][9]. Race packs at the debut were distributed over a two-day collection window at Bahtoo Gymnasium, and organisers explicitly reserve the right to change the date, venue or programme without prior notice — worth bookmarking if you're flying in [3][8].

Minors need a signed parental consent form at pack collection, and registration confirmation only lands after payment and a confirmation email, so last-minute sign-ups carry some administrative risk [2].

sections.heading: Atmosphere, Scale and the Prize Purse
paragraphs: This is part of a bigger comeback story. The Yoma Marathon began in 2013, went quiet for five years through COVID, and returned in 2026 as the 9th overall edition — the first time the series expanded beyond Yangon to add Mandalay [4][5]. AmCham Myanmar's own framing was blunt: "The Yoma Marathon is back — bigger and better than ever!" [5]

Prize money at the debut was substantial for a regional half marathon, with the men's and women's half marathon winners taking K3 million down to K5 million for fourth through tenth, and the challenge run paying out from K1.5 million downward — enough to draw serious local competitors, not just charity joggers [3].

For a read on scale, the sister Yangon race a month later pulled over 7,000 runners back to the National Indoor Stadium after its own five-year layoff, complete with a full awards ceremony and finisher medals for everyone inside the cut-off [7]. Mandalay's own event page has run a runner counter alongside the phrase "12K runners," hinting at the field size organisers are building toward [1].

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If you want a half marathon (or 10K/5K) that doubles as a first look at Mandalay's streets, with organisers promising you'll "experience the charm of Mandalay" along the route, this fits the bill for a travel-and-run trip [1]. It's also a reasonable target for competitive Myanmar-based runners given the prize structure carried over from the debut [3].

The caveats are honest ones: this is only the race's second Mandalay outing, the exact 2026 start venue is still unpublished, and the organiser has explicitly reserved the right to alter details without notice — so build in flexibility rather than locking flights the moment you register [1][8].

Bottom line: a promising, still-forming event backed by Myanmar's most established marathon brand, best suited to adventurous half-marathon and 10K runners who don't need a decade of race-day polish to have a good time.

faqs.question: When is the Yoma Mandalay International Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: The edition covered in this review is scheduled for December 6, 2026, following the race's debut Mandalay outing held in January 2026 at Bahtoo Stadium. Runners should check the official site for final confirmation as details can change.

faqs.question: What distances can I run?
faqs.answer: Three categories: a 21km half marathon, a 10km challenge run, and a 5km fun run, all starting and finishing near the host stadium according to the debut edition's race info, with routes passing landmark sites around Mandalay.

faqs.question: Where does the race start and finish?
faqs.answer: The January 2026 debut used Bahtoo Stadium as start and finish, but the exact start point for the December 2026 edition has not yet been published, so confirm via the official race guide closer to the date.

faqs.question: Is there prize money?
faqs.answer: Yes — the debut half marathon paid K3 million for first place down to K5 million for fourth through tenth, with the 10km challenge run paying from K1.5 million downward for men's and women's category winners.
